title: TSMC OIP: Chip Industry Growth Blows Past Forecast
gist: At TSMC's OIP symposium, TSMC said the semiconductor industry will reach ~$1.7T by end of 2026 with >$1T from AI alone, blowing past its own 2024 forecast of ~$1T by 2030; TSMC revenue is up 53.3% YoY in August, N2 new tape-outs are surging, inference tokens have grown 500x in three years, and AI-driven design is compressing ASIC cycles.

insights.claim: TSMC North America CEO Sajiv Dalal said the semiconductor industry will reach about $1.7T by end of 2026, with more than $1T coming from AI alone.
insights.speaker: Barry Pangrle
insights.so_what: AI now represents the majority of semiconductor revenue, concentrating industry exposure to AI capex.
insights.locator: At this year’s OIC, TSMC North America

insights.claim: In January 2024 TSMC's Kevin Zhang forecast worldwide semiconductor revenue reaching ~$1T by 2030, a forecast the author says was $700B too low given 2026 levels.
insights.speaker: Barry Pangrle
insights.so_what: Shows how badly consensus underestimated AI-driven demand, a caution for current forecasts.
insights.quote: Aggressive prediction of $1T by 2030 was $700B too low.

insights.claim: Dalal's ~$1.7T industry forecast is broadly in line with Gartner's forecast of ~$1.6T for 2026.
insights.speaker: Barry Pangrle
insights.so_what: Independent corroboration of the size of the 2026 chip market.
insights.quote: in line with Gartner’s forecast of ~$1.6T for the industry in 2026
insights.locator: At this year’s OIC, TSMC North America

insights.claim: The author says AI semiconductor spending has been accelerating at a ferocious pace.
insights.speaker: Barry Pangrle
insights.so_what: Momentum in AI chip spending supports foundry, memory and packaging names.
insights.quote: The surge in AI semiconductor spending has been accelerating at a ferocious pace.
insights.locator: At this year’s OIC, TSMC North America

insights.claim: TSMC's August 2026 revenue was up 53.3% year-over-year, and January-August 2026 revenue was up 39.3% versus the same period of 2025.
insights.speaker: Barry Pangrle
insights.so_what: Hard data on TSMC's accelerating top line.

insights.claim: TSMC's Li-Pen Yuan said new tape-outs have increased 4x when measured in the second year of a technology across N5, N3 and N2, with N2 seeing a massive acceleration in new designs beyond N3's rate.
insights.speaker: Barry Pangrle
insights.so_what: Strong N2 design pipeline points to sustained leading-edge wafer demand and pricing power.

insights.claim: TSMC's L.C. Lu said inference token usage has grown 500x over the past three years and that inference is becoming the growth driver for AI.
insights.speaker: Barry Pangrle
insights.so_what: Shift from training to inference broadens and sustains AI chip demand.
insights.quote: inference token usage has grown 500× over the past three years

insights.claim: The AI build-out is increasingly making new demands on compute, memory density and power.
insights.speaker: Barry Pangrle
insights.so_what: Power and memory are the bottlenecks to watch for supplier opportunity.

insights.claim: L.C. Lu said power scaling extends Moore's Law; TSMC's A14 Nanoflex uses a 1.5x cell height (vs. 2x previously) and delivers 14% speed improvement and 23% power reduction versus N2P.
insights.speaker: Barry Pangrle
insights.so_what: Quantifies the A14 node's PPA gain, key to TSMC's continued leadership.
insights.quote: Lu noted that power scaling extends Moore’s Law.

insights.claim: TSMC shows HPC cell power efficiency improving 2.3x going from N3P to A12 SPR.
insights.speaker: Barry Pangrle
insights.so_what: Power efficiency gains are central to data center TCO under power constraints.

insights.claim: TSMC predicts its memory figure of merit (transistors x speed@power) will rise 87x by 2029, with HBM bandwidth up 34x, 3D DRAM 115x and SRAM 830x over five years.
insights.speaker: Barry Pangrle
insights.so_what: Signals where memory innovation and spend will concentrate through 2029.
insights.quote: In five years, bandwidths for HBM will increase 34×, 3D DRAM 115×, and SRAM by 830×.
insights.locator: For memory, Lu presented a figure

insights.claim: TSMC forecasts 2029 energy per bit of 0.32pJ/bit for SRAM, 1pJ/bit for 3D DRAM and 2.5pJ/bit for HBM.
insights.speaker: Barry Pangrle
insights.so_what: Energy-per-bit gap favors on-die and 3D memory integration over HBM long term.
insights.locator: For memory, Lu presented a figure

insights.claim: TSMC-COUPE targets higher bandwidth at lower energy per bit as serial data rates jump to 224G and 448G, with a roadmap using multiple wavelengths per fiber to raise fiber capacity.
insights.speaker: Barry Pangrle
insights.so_what: TSMC is positioning in co-packaged optics, relevant to optical interconnect supply chain.

insights.claim: Broadcom's Greg Dix said OpenAI's Jalapeno custom AI ASIC went from project kick-off to tape-out in just nine months.
insights.speaker: Barry Pangrle
insights.so_what: Shows custom ASIC cycles shrinking, strengthening the custom-silicon model for hyperscalers.
insights.locator: AI is now acting in a positive

insights.claim: Broadcom's Greg Dix said the SoC era is ending and SiP is accelerating.
insights.speaker: Barry Pangrle
insights.so_what: Favors advanced packaging and chiplet suppliers over monolithic SoC approaches.
insights.quote: the SoC era is ending and SiP is accelerating
insights.locator: AI is now acting in a positive

insights.claim: AI is in a positive feedback loop where advances in AI create new tools and productivity for developing new AI technologies, with TSMC supplying AI Design Kits (ADK) for AI-driven design flows.
insights.speaker: Barry Pangrle
insights.so_what: AI-for-chip-design accelerates the cadence of AI hardware itself.
insights.quote: AI is now acting in a positive feedback environment
insights.locator: AI is now acting in a positive

insights.claim: TSMC added imec as a partner; IC-Link by imec, AWS and Microsoft Azure won cloud partner awards, while Cadence, Siemens EDA and Synopsys won EDA partner of the year.
insights.speaker: Barry Pangrle
insights.so_what: Confirms the EDA and cloud vendors embedded in TSMC's ecosystem.
